rule: Working branch never tracks trunk, and the first PR push sets the branch's own upstream
description: `plugin/skills/create-working-branch/SKILL.md` requirement 6 is the source for the rule that a newly created working branch carries no upstream: it is created from `base` with `git switch --no-track -c`, because creating it from a remote-tracking base such as `origin/main` would otherwise make it track trunk, letting a plain `git push` or a force-with-lease retry against the tracked upstream target trunk. The source pin is ONE span carrying both the condition (the working branch does NOT yet exist) and the obligation (create it from `base` via `git switch --no-track -c <working_branch> <base>`); dropping `--no-track` or rewriting either half turns the suite red. Two consumers keep the rule closed at its two other points. In the same file, the existing-branch path must still carry the clause that, after `git switch <working_branch>`, an upstream whose name is not `<remote>/<working_branch>` is removed with `git branch --unset-upstream`; that pin spans both the mismatch condition and the unset obligation. In `plugin/skills/open-plan-pr/SKILL.md` step 6, the no-upstream, no-`push_remote` branch must still carry the clause that, when `git config --get remote.origin.url` succeeds, the skill runs `git push -u origin "HEAD:$b"` with `b` captured from `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, so the branch's first push sets an upstream named after the branch itself; that pin spans both the origin-present condition and the push command. What these pins honestly guarantee is exactly that these three word sequences exist in these two named files; they claim nothing about meaning. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) the fenced Bash block that implements the unset-upstream comparison in create-working-branch is NOT pinned, so a rewrite of that block that no longer compares against `refs/remotes/$rem/$b` stays green while the prose clause survives; (2) the open-plan-pr failure handling (warn and continue to step 7) and the no-origin deferral to `gh pr create` are outside the pinned span; (3) a meaning inversion around the pinned bytes, such as surrounding prose that makes the unset or the push optional, is invisible; (4) the pins see only the two files they name, and no fixture in this directory can detect a NEW branch-creating or PR-opening skill that never carries these clauses, which is an absence defect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract.

source.pattern: if `working_branch` does NOT yet exist, create it from `base` via `git switch --no-track -c <working_branch> <base>`

consumers.pattern: After `git switch <working_branch>`, if an upstream is set and its name is not `<remote>/<working_branch>`, run `git branch --unset-upstream`.
else (no upstream, no `push_remote`): when `git config --get remote.origin.url` succeeds, run `b="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"; git push -u origin "HEAD:$b"`
